headline: 255 votes: Mirza Fakhrul elected as Bangladesh's 23rd president
summary: The BNP leader wins a contested parliamentary vote, ending a 35-year gap since the last such election for the presidency.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh after securing 255 votes in the National Parliament. This marks the first contested presidential election by MPs in 35 years.
His opponent, Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, received 88 votes. Out of 349 total voters, 343 cast valid votes, while 6 ballots remained unused.
The voting and public counting took place on Thursday at the National Parliament building. Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin officially announced the results following the process.

Following the announcement, BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated Fakhrul with a red rose. Members of both the government and opposition parties also extended their congratulations to the new head of state.

Fakhrul's victory was largely expected as the BNP holds more than two-thirds of the seats in Parliament. He had stepped down from his role as Secretary General of the BNP after the party officially nominated him on August 13.
In an emotional farewell post on Facebook, Fakhrul bid goodbye to his political role, stating it was time for his final departure and shouting 'Bangladesh Nationalist Party Zindabad' one last time.
The official gazette for the election result is expected to be published today. Mirza Fakhrul is scheduled to take the oath of office tomorrow, Friday.
caption:
After 35 years, Bangladesh holds a contested presidential vote. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir wins with 255 votes to become the 23rd President.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh after securing 255 votes in the National Parliament. This marks the first contested presidential election by MPs in 35 years.

His opponent, Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, received 88 votes. Out of 349 total voters, 343 cast valid votes, while 6 ballots remained unused.

The voting and public counting took place on Thursday at the National Parliament building. Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin officially announced the results following the process.

Following the announcement, BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated Fakhrul with a red rose. Members of both the government and opposition parties also extended their congratulations to the new head of state.

Fakhrul's victory was largely expected as the BNP holds more than two-thirds of the seats in Parliament. He had stepped down from his role as Secretary General of the BNP after the party officially nominated him on August 13.

In an emotional farewell post on Facebook, Fakhrul bid goodbye to his political role, stating it was time for his final departure and shouting 'Bangladesh Nationalist Party Zindabad' one last time.

The official gazette for the election result is expected to be published today. Mirza Fakhrul is scheduled to take the oath of office tomorrow, Friday.

headline_marked: 750 cases in 24 hours: [[One dies as dengue cases surge]]
headline: 750 cases in 24 hours: One dies as dengue cases surge
summary: One person has died and 750 new cases were recorded in a single day, prompting the DSCC to initiate legal action against those allowing mosquito larvae to breed.
details: One person has died and 750 new dengue cases were recorded within the last 24 hours, according to recent reports.
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has announced the start of legal action to combat the outbreak.
The DSCC administrator stated that strict measures will be taken against property owners or residents if mosquito larvae are found on their premises.
This move comes as the city struggles to contain the spread of the virus during the peak season.
